calls.head: Expect the Penguins to fire from everywhere
calls.body: The Penguins shoot a lot, and the Capitals are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.
calls.call: The Penguins take at least their usual 60.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Pittsburgh 8th for shot volume (60.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Washington 24th for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Pittsburgh took 59.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 60.2.

calls.head: The Penguins should get some good looks
calls.body: The Penguins make their shots count, and the Capitals are around the middle of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Penguins to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Penguins’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Pittsburgh 7th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Washington 22nd for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Pittsburgh’s average shot had an 8.9% chance of going in, against their usual 6.7%.
calls.beyond: Pittsburgh’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: an 8.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

calls.head: Nobody’s sitting back in this one
calls.body: Pittsburgh plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Washington. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 84.2 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Pittsburgh 6th (84.2), Washington 9th (83.3)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 88.7 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 84.2 and a league average of 81.8.

calls.head: Airtight against leaky on the kill
calls.body: On the penalty kill, Pittsburgh is near the top of the league and Washington is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Penguins’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Capitals’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill, Pittsburgh had 8.3 per 60 and Washington 9.4 per 60. Coming in, Pittsburgh was at 6.9 per 60 and Washington at 8.1 per 60.

WSH.head: We had this close to even (45% for Washington), and Washington came through.

PIT.head: We had this close to even (55% for Pittsburgh), and it went Washington’s way.

surprises.head: Pittsburgh hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Pittsburgh’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 31, against their usual 72 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

surprises.head: Washington tried a different line
surprises.body: B. Jenner, J. Sourdif, R. Leonard played 8:40 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Washington’s usual lines.

story.head: The Capitals beat the Penguins
paras: Anthony Beauvillier opened the scoring 23 seconds in. Five different Capitals scored. Alex Tuch scored the winner midway through the second.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. By our Swing measure, Pierre-Luc Dubois had the best night of anyone. The Capitals tried a line they hadn’t used before: Boone Jenner, Justin Sourdif and Ryan Leonard.

items.text: Whether the Capitals keep that line together at home against the Rangers on Friday.
Three of the preview’s four calls held.
